facts.statement: Cedrorestes is known from an incomplete skeleton found in the Valanginian-age Yellow Cat Member of the Cedar Mountain Formation.
facts.quote: It is based on an incomplete skeleton which was found in the Valanginian-age Yellow Cat Member of the Cedar Mountain Formation.

facts.statement: The remains of Cedrorestes were recovered in 2001 from the top of the Yellow Cat Member in east-central Utah.
facts.quote: These remains were in 2001 recovered from near the top of the Yellow Cat Member of the Cedar Mountain Formation, in east-central Utah.

facts.statement: The type specimen DMNH 47994 is a partial skeleton containing rib fragments, a sacrum, ilia, a thighbone, a metatarsal, and ossified tendon fragments.
facts.quote: Cedrorestes is based on DMNH 47994, a partial skeleton including rib fragments, a sacrum, the left ilium and a portion of the right, a right thighbone, the right third metatarsal, and fragments of ossified tendons.

facts.statement: The generic name Cedrorestes means "mountain cedar dweller," derived from the formation where it was found.
facts.quote: The etymology of the generic name is, from Latin, cedrus (cedr-); "cedar" + Greek oros-; "mountain", after the Cedar Mountain formation, where the fossil was found + Greek suffix ending -etes; "dweller".

facts.statement: The species name crichtoni honors author Michael Crichton, who wrote Jurassic Park and The Lost World.
facts.quote: The specific epithet crichtoni is after Michael Crichton, author of Jurassic Park and The Lost World.

facts.statement: The genus was originally classified in Hadrosauridae as the earliest known member of that family.
facts.quote: They placed their new genus in Hadrosauridae, as the earliest known hadrosaurid.

facts.statement: Cedrorestes is distinguished by a combination of a tall ilium like Iguanodon and a large lateral bony process near the hip joint typical of hadrosaurids.
facts.quote: Este género se aparta de otros iguanodontia por la combinación de un ilion alto como en el Iguanodon, con un largo proceso anatómico lateral sobre y a los lados del acetábulo y una superficie de contacto con el isquion, que se ve en los hadrosáuridos.

facts.statement: Researchers placed the genus within Hadrosauridae as a basal member.
facts.quote: Ellos colocaron al nuevo género dentro de Hadrosauridae, como un miembro basal.

facts.statement: Cedrorestes lived during the Early Cretaceous period in Utah.
facts.quote: Cedrorestes is a genus of iguanodontian dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of Utah.

facts.statement: Cedrorestes lived during the Barremian stage of the Early Cretaceous, approximately 130 to 125 million years ago, in what is now North America.
facts.quote: un dinosaurio ornitópodo hadrosauriforme que vivió a principios del período Cretácico en el Barremiense, hace aproximadamente entre 130 y 125 millones de años en lo que es hoy Norteamérica.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence places Cedrorestes in the Valanginian stage between 137.05 and 132.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Valanginian to Valanginian (137.05 to 132.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: Cedrorestes was estimated to be about 6 meters long and weigh 1500 kilograms.
facts.quote: Pudiendo ser un hadrosáurido basal o un derivado no-hadrosáurido iguanodóntido, Cedrorestes fue un gran herbívoro de alrededor de 6 metros de largo y 1500 kilogramos de peso, capaz de moverse como bípedo o cuadrúpedo.

facts.statement: The hip structure suggests hadrosaurid-like leg muscles, but the functional differences in movement compared to iguanodontians remain unclear.
facts.quote: The structure of its hip indicates that it had hadrosaurid-like leg muscles, but the functional significance of the changes in leg muscles from the iguanodontian layout to the hadrosaurid layout, and resulting differences in movement (if any), are not yet understood.

facts.statement: Cedrorestes lived alongside other dinosaurs including the theropod Utahraptor, the sauropod Cedarosaurus, and the armored dinosaur Gastonia.
facts.quote: El Miembro Yellow Cat de la Formación Cedar Mountain es conocida por varios dinosaurios que incluyen al terópodo celurosauriano nedcolbertia, al dromeosáurido utahraptor, saurópodo braquiosáurido cedarosaurio, y al pesadamente armado anquilosáurido gastonia.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Cedrorestes represents a basal hadrosaurid or a derived non-hadrosaurid iguanodontian.
facts.quote: Whether a basal hadrosaurid or derived non-hadrosaurid iguanodontian, Cedrorestes would have been a large herbivore capable of moving both bipedally or on all fours.

facts.statement: While hip structures suggest hadrosaurid-like muscles, the specific differences in movement compared to iguanodontians are not yet clear.
facts.quote: Las estructuras de las caderas indican que tenía una estructura muscular similar a la de los hadrosáuridos, pero las diferencias en los movimientos con los iguanodóntidos, si hay alguna no son claras aún.

rejected.statement: The fossils were found scattered in calcareous mudstone and show evidence of pre-burial damage from weathering or trampling.
rejected.quote: They were found scattered in a calcareous mudstone, and showed evidence of pre-burial damage, from weathering or trampling.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'evidence of pre-burial damage from weathering or trampling'

rejected.statement: Researchers David Gilpin and colleagues described the genus in 2007 and placed it near the evolutionary split between hadrosaurids and iguanodontids.
rejected.quote: David Gilpin and his coauthors, who described the specimen, noted that the lateral process has been considered diagnostic for hadrosaurids, and interpreted the combination of anatomical characteristics in Cedrorestes as evidence that the genus was close to the division between hadrosaurids and iguanodontids.

rejected.statement: Cedrorestes was a large herbivore capable of moving both bipedally and quadrupedally.
rejected.quote: Whether a basal hadrosaurid or derived non-hadrosaurid iguanodontian, Cedrorestes would have been a large herbivore capable of moving both bipedally or on all fours.
